clinician.final_diagnosis: Heterotopic pregnancy (simultaneous intrauterine and ectopic pregnancy)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old female with infertility history underwent fertility treatment with clomiphene and intrauterine insemination. She presented to the ED with acute onset right lower quadrant pain and vomiting following intercourse. Morning outpatient ultrasound revealed a gestational sac in the uterus, a cystic mass in the right adnexa, and pelvic free fluid, raising concern for heterotopic pregnancy. ED POCUS demonstrated significant increase in abdominal bleeding compared to the outpatient ultrasound performed an hour prior, indicating rupture of the ectopic component. Physical examination showed RLQ tenderness without peritoneal signs. ED vital signs showed mild tachycardia (HR 109 bpm) but otherwise stable hemodynamics (BP 114/65, RR 21, O2 sat 100% RA, temp 36.7°C). Exploratory laparoscopy confirmed the diagnosis, revealing a right fallopian tube dilated due to ectopic pregnancy with a 1 cm paratubal cyst. Right salpingectomy was performed with evacuation of 100 mL of intra-abdominal blood. The procedure was completed without complications, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 1.
